content.intro: This lesson develops topic 18 of the supplied curriculum: **Array Size and Item Size**. The main starting point is **The size  attribute**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Shape describes how values are arranged; dtype describes how values are represented. Inspecting both before an operation catches many mistakes early.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Array Size and Item Size** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **The size  attribute** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.title: Subtopics from the supplied curriculum
items: Number of elements versus bytes per element

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

arr = np.array([1, 2, 3], dtype=np.int32)
print(arr.size, arr.itemsize, arr.nbytes)

common_mistakes.why: Size counts elements; shape describes axis lengths.
Slicing and transposing can produce non-contiguous views.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect `flags` and `strides` when memory layout matters.
